reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown distinguish God as an impartial judge who ignores status from God as a sovereign giver who freely favored Abel's offering over Cain's.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells sets Genesis 4:4's claim that Yahweh respected Abel over Cain against the stack of Deuteronomy, Chronicles, Acts, Romans, Galatians, Ephesians, Colossians, and 1 Peter texts declaring that God shows no partiality.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013).

sides.snippet: Yahweh respected Abel and his offering
sides.verseText: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of the fat of it. Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,

sides.snippet: For there is no partiality with God.
sides.verseText: For there is no partiality with God.
